## GET /admin-api/ldap

`getLdapSettings`

**The embedded directory's own settings**

The six `ldap.*` settings: the two raw ports, the base DN, whether a name seen for the first time gets an entry, and the two ceilings that keep it from being filled up.

NOTHING HERE REFUSES A BIND, and no setting is missing: the MODE decides. In development any DN with any password, and anonymous, are accepted on 389 and 636 alike; in product only a person binds, on 636, with a password verified against their entry. There is no such behaviour to turn on.

The base DN is the DEFAULT realm's directory and every other realm is a subtree beneath it, because a socket has no path to put a realm segment in and a DN is the one name a client can carry. What is IN the directory is `GET /users` and `GET /groups`.

THERE IS NO POST BESIDE THIS ONE and that is not a gap: every form on the console page this mirrors posts `set-many` to /admin/config, so `POST /admin-api/config/set-many` is already the operation for it. One store, one action, two doors.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/ldap` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

## GET /admin-api/ldap/applications

`getDirectoryApplications`

**The application registry as the directory holds it, and its schema**

One entry per identifier under `ou=applications`, every attribute on it, and the published SCHEMA — the object classes and every attribute name with what sets it.

THE SCHEMA IS WHY THIS IS NOT `GET /admin-api/applications`. That operation is the registry as the console works with it: the counters, the drill-down, the writes. This is the registry as the DIRECTORY holds it, and the vocabulary is the half a client reading an entry back over 389 actually needs — this directory is schemaless, so an entry carrying thirty invented attribute names is otherwise guesswork.

THESE ENTRIES ARE THE REGISTRY rather than a copy of one. Nothing caches them, so an `ldapmodify` of `oauthRedirectUri` changes which redirect URI RFC 9700 mode accepts on the next request.

Two attributes hold CREDENTIALS in the clear, for the reason the development Kerberos passwords are printed as settings. They are never written to the audit log.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/ldap/applications` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |

## GET /admin-api/ldap/devices

`getDirectoryDevices`

**The device register as the directory holds it, and its schema**

One entry per device under `ou=devices`, every attribute on it, and the SCHEMA `common/devices.ts` publishes. A key, the last compliance and status change and the enrolment are ONE JSON VALUE each. `stsDeviceSecretHash` is withheld, as from every LDAP read; every other value is shown as the directory holds it. Read-only: the register is edited through `/admin-api/devices`.

WHERE THE DIRECTORY IS A WINDOW (#359) the count and the page are asked of the store, and a `q` looks inside at most a bounded number of entries and says so in `search`. A page past the walk's cap (100,000 entries) is empty and carries `pageCap`.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/ldap/devices` on the admin console.

## GET /admin-api/ldap/directory

`getDirectoryEntries`

**Every entry in this realm's directory, paged**

The whole store, DN by DN, with where each entry came from — `seed`, an LDAP `add`, or an authentication — and every attribute with every value.

IT IS NOT AN LDAP SEARCH. This is the service showing its own store, which is how a caller tells an empty directory from a filter that matched nothing, and it is why the operational attributes are here: a search withholds `createTimestamp` and `modifyTimestamp` unless they are asked for by name (RFC 4511 §4.5.1.8) and this is not a search.

`q` matches the DN, any attribute NAME and any attribute VALUE, case-insensitively — values because the caller who needs this most often has a thumbprint or a secret in hand and no idea which entry carries it.

WHERE THE DIRECTORY IS HELD AS A WINDOW ONTO THE STORE (#616) the counts, the `origin` filter, the order and the page are asked of the store, so the order is the store's key order (`order: key`), and a `q` — which matches values the store holds sealed — looks inside at most a bounded number of entries and says how many in `search`.

THE REPLY IS THIS REALM'S DIRECTORY AND NO OTHER. Since 2026-08-25 each trust realm has a subtree of its own; reach another realm's through its own path prefix.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/ldap/directory` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `q` | query | string |  | Substring of the DN, of an attribute name, or of an attribute value. Case-insensitive. |
| `origin` | query | string |  | Only entries that came from here. The values actually present are in `origins`. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## GET /admin-api/ldap/federations

`getDirectoryFederations`

**The federation register as the directory holds it, and its schema**

The application registry's twin, for `ou=federations` — and THE ONE CONTAINER IN THIS DIRECTORY WHERE AN LDAPMODIFY IS A SECURITY CHANGE. Everywhere else an edit changes what this service HANDS OUT; `fedSigningCertificate` decides whose assertions it will BELIEVE and `fedEnabled` turns a partner on.

It is a container of its own rather than a corner of `ou=applications` because half its entries are FOREIGN IDENTITY PROVIDERS, which ask this service for nothing at all.

The schema carries a column the applications one has no need of: which DIRECTION each attribute is for.

`fedClientSecret` is REDACTED in `relationships` and present in the entry's own attributes, which is the same split the page makes: what a script reads is redacted, and a page claiming to say what the directory holds may not hide a value an `ldapsearch` shows.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/ldap/federations` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `q` | query | string |  | Substring of the relationship id, the DN, the protocol or the direction. Case-insensitive. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**200**: The page of relationships, the roles, the protocols and the schema.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |

## GET /admin-api/ldap/peps

`getDirectoryPeps`

**The registered remote PEPs as the directory holds them, and their schema**

ALMOST EVERYTHING IN THIS CONTAINER IS A RECORD rather than configuration, which is what it has in common with `ou=agents` next door. A PEP registers itself, and its identity is taken from the CLIENT CERTIFICATE it presented and never from the body it sent.

Two attributes are not a record and an `ldapmodify` of either is a real change: `xacmlPepEnabled` is an administrator's decision and a PEP that reconnects does not clear it, and `xacmlPepNotifyUrl` is one of the three addresses this service will dial.

**AN EMPTY `peps` ARRAY IS NOT A FEATURE THAT IS OFF.** A remote PEP pulls `GET /xacml/pep/policies` and converges without registering at all; registering is what buys it the change nudge and a row on the console.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/ldap/peps` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `q` | query | string |  | Substring of a PEP name, a DN, or any value on the entry — a certificate subject or a notify URL included. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**200**: The page of registered PEPs and the schema.

## GET /admin-api/ldap/policies

`getDirectoryPolicies`

**The policy repository as the directory holds it, and its schema**

`ou=policies` IS the XACML policy repository, the way `ou=federations` is the federation register. One entry per policy or policy set, holding the document itself, with exactly one of them the root — a PDP evaluates one document and reaches the rest through PolicyIdReference.

**A WRITE HERE SKIPS THE TYPECHECKER, and that is the one thing this operation says that `GET /admin-api/xacml/policies` does not.** Every write through the console and through /admin-api/xacml parses the document and statically typechecks it, so a policy that does not typecheck is refused at WRITE time rather than going Indeterminate on every request. An `ldapmodify` of `xacmlPolicyDocument` reaches the entry directly and skips all of it, and nothing caches these entries.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/ldap/policies` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `q` | query | string |  | Substring of a policy name, a DN, or any value on the entry — the DOCUMENT included, so this finds the policy that names a particular resource. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**200**: The page of policy entries and the schema.

## GET /admin-api/ldap/roles

`getDirectoryRoles`

**The role entries as the directory holds them, and their schema**

THIS CONTAINER IS HALF THE FEATURE. A role has two relations and they are stored apart on purpose: MEMBERSHIP — who holds it — is here on the role entry, and the REQUIREMENT — which roles an application demands before anything is issued for it — is `appRequiredRole` on the APPLICATION entry, under a different container. So nothing in this reply refuses anybody by itself, and a caller looking for the reason somebody was turned away wants `GET /admin-api/roles`, which resolves both halves.

**THE SIX BUILT-IN ROLES ARE IN NO CONTAINER.** They are computed from the context of the decision being made, so `EVERYBODY` has no entry here and never will — which is why an empty `roles` array is the ORDINARY state of a service refusing nobody rather than a sign that the feature is not loaded.

THE ENTRIES ARE THE REGISTER: nothing caches them, so an `ldapmodify` adding a value to `roleMemberUser` is answered by the very next issuance decision.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/ldap/roles` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `q` | query | string |  | Substring of a role name, a DN, or any value on the entry — which includes its members, so this is how to find the roles one person holds by name. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## GET /admin-api/ldap/service

`getDirectoryService`

**What the embedded directory IS, right now**

The two raw sockets and the store behind them AS THEY ACTUALLY ARE: whether TCP 389 and LDAPS 636 really bound and the error if either did not, the base DN and each realm's naming context, what a subtree search from each one answers about, the bind policy, the four structural rules this directory does still enforce, the entry count and the persistence status.

WHY IT IS NOT `GET /admin-api/ldap`: that operation is the six `ldap.*` SETTINGS — what the sockets are configured to be. This one is what happened. A host whose own slapd already holds 389 makes the two disagree, and nothing else in this service can report that: `/admin/sts-metadata` is built by walking the express router and a raw TCP listener is not on it.

NO BIND IS EVER REFUSED here, by any setting, except the one literal password named in `refusedPassword` — which exists so a negative test has something to fail on.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/ldap/service` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

## GET /admin-api/ldap/spiffe

`getDirectorySpiffe`

**The two SPIFFE containers as the directory holds them, and their schema**

THE TWO CONTAINERS HOLD DIFFERENT KINDS OF THING, which is why they are two. `ou=entries` is CONFIGURATION — which SPIFFE ID a workload gets, under which parent, matching which selectors — and `ou=agents` is a RECORD of what has attested, which is why nothing about an agent is editable anywhere.

THE ENTRIES ARE THE REGISTRY: nothing caches them, so an `ldapmodify` of `spiffeX509SvidTtl` changes the lifetime of the next SVID the Workload API hands out.

THIS IS THE ONE DIRECTORY OPERATION WITH TWO LISTS IN IT, so it pages the way the console's drill-downs do: `entriesPage` and `agentsPage` move one list each and `per` is shared, with an `entriesPaging` and an `agentsPaging` object in the reply. `entries` and `agents` at the top level are the TOTALS and not the page.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/ldap/spiffe` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entryq` | query | string |  | Substring of a registration entry's SPIFFE ID or DN. |
| `agentq` | query | string |  | Substring of an attested agent's id or DN. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `entriesPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `entries` to return, answered by `entriesPaging`. The registration entries. |
| `agentsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `agents` to return, answered by `agentsPaging`. The attested agents. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**200**: The two pages, the two containers and the schema.
